newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ invokes WTO dispute procedure in EU butter row.
newsitem.headline: NZ invokes WTO dispute procedure in EU butter row.

text.p: New Zealand said on Monday it was asking the European Union for formal dispute settlement consultations under the World Trade Organisation in a row over its exports of spreadable butter to the EU.

The move followed an EU decision to exclude New Zealand butter manufactured by the modern spreadable and AMMIX processes from eligibility for reduced duties under New Zealand's WTO quota access to the EU.
AMMIX is a process used to split cream into fat and fluid, and can be used to produce a soft butter which is easier to spread than traditional butter.
"The EU's decision is a clear breach of the obligations which it owes New Zealand under the WTO agreement," Trade Minister Lockwood Smith said in a statement.

A Dairy Board spokesman said the cost to New Zealand of the EU action was about NZ$10 million (US$6.9 million) per year, because it would need to get the spreadable product made in Europe instead of domestically.
He said the industry had invested about NZ$75 million in plant, equipment, packaging and marketing of spreadable butter.
The EU argues that spreadable and AMMIX butter are not made directly from milk or cream, but Smith said: "I have no doubt at all that these New Zealand products meet this criteria."
"We have made intensive efforts to resolve this issue through bilateral contacts. I regret that these have failed to break the impasse between New Zealand and the EU," he added.
If the EU decision stood unchanged, it would restrict the New Zealand dairy industry's ability to take advantage of technological progress in the the future, Smith said. NZ$1 = US$0.69
